statusText: Calm, wait-and-see conditions persist into the European late-morning ahead of today's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales / 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich data cluster. This run's WebSearch again returned the identical Nasdaq 100 futures print (~30,177.50, range 30,124.25-30,232.00) as the prior three runs -- now a fourth consecutive stale/cached snapshot rather than a fresh intraday read, a genuine live-evidence limitation. VIX holds flat near 14.4-14.7. Iran-Oman Hormuz talks remain unresolved and conditional (Iran continues to withhold full reopening pending US concessions/compensation) -- progress-in-talks, not a resolved discontinuity, and no new kinetic escalation was identified this run. Semiconductors firmed overnight (Samsung, SK Hynix higher; Nvidia reversed higher in premarket) with no negative index-level catalyst. Alpha Vantage remains fully rate-limited for an eighth consecutive run (TREASURY_YIELD retried once, both attempts returned an immediate rate_limit error), so this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch; combined with the now four-times-repeated stale futures snapshot, Confidence eases further into the low band this run.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Continue monitoring through the late European morning and into the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales and 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich sentiment cluster; an upgrade to a higher Tail state still requires observed persistent one-way structure with failed pullbacks in the broad Nasdaq-100 complex itself, not the pending data cluster, the unresolved Hormuz talks, or this run's continued Alpha Vantage outage and repeated stale futures print.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures print unchanged for a fourth straight run in WebSearch results (stale snapshot, no fresh intraday structure confirmed); VIX flat near 14.4-14.7; Iran-Oman Hormuz talks remain unresolved/conditional with no new kinetic escalation; semiconductors firm overnight (Samsung, SK Hynix, Nvidia premarket) with no negative catalyst; today's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales and 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich sentiment remain the session's main checkpoints; Alpha Vantage remains fully rate-limited for an eighth consecutive run, so Confidence eases further into the low band.
body: About 35-40 minutes past the top of the hour, conditions remain calm into the European late morning, roughly one hour on from the prior run. This run's WebSearch results for Nasdaq 100 futures again returned the identical price level and session range as the prior three runs (~30,177.50, range 30,124.25-30,232.00) -- now a fourth consecutive stale/cached snapshot rather than a fresh intraday print, a genuine live price-path limitation this run, distinct from asserting the structure itself. VIX holds flat near 14.4-14.7, essentially unchanged from the prior run. The 10-year Treasury yield continues to hold near its recent range (~4.65-4.66%, last reliably observed Thursday), consistent with prior runs and not indicating fresh repricing; Alpha Vantage TREASURY_YIELD was unavailable this run (see below). On the Strait of Hormuz, Iran continues to withhold a full reopening pending US concessions and compensation even as Oman-brokered talks are reported "very close" on managing the waterway -- this remains progress-in-talks rather than a resolved discontinuity, consistent with the prior run's framing, and no new kinetic escalation was identified this run. Semiconductors firmed overnight: South Korean chip names (Samsung, SK Hynix) rallied sharply and Nvidia reversed higher in premarket trading after the prior session's pullback, with no negative index-level semiconductor catalyst identified; Nvidia's Aug 26 earnings remain the next dedicated catalyst. CoreWeave's post-earnings pop (+~14% on a strong AI-cloud revenue beat) is a positive single-name AI datapoint but not itself Nasdaq-100 index-level structure. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota remains exhausted for an eighth consecutive run -- the TREASURY_YIELD call was retried once and returned an immediate rate_limit error both times -- so, per the fallback protocol, this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch for yields, oil, VIX, equities and price-path context. Combined with the now four-times-repeated identical/stale futures print, evidence quality has degraded further this run, and Confidence eases to 37 (low, down from 38) to reflect that. Tail holds at 9% (still low; no persistent one-way structure evidence, and calm overnight/morning conditions are not themselves a Nasdaq-100 price-path signal) while Stress eases slightly to 25% (moderate, down from 26%) on the absence of any fresh negative catalyst, with the main forecast driver remaining the pending 12:30 UTC Retail Sales / 14:00 UTC UMich cluster, which is projected to push Stress higher into midday UTC before easing back through the afternoon, evening, and into the quiet Saturday handover.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (9-18%) through the full prior 24 hours as the index ground to a fresh S&P 500 record above 7,800 on soft PPI; Stress ran elevated to high (up to 58%) around the Wednesday/Thursday CPI-PPI and AMAT-earnings window before easing back into the low-to-moderate band (23-29%) by Friday's European morning as the after-hours reaction stayed contained to the single name and no broader transmission was confirmed.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (5-11%) through the next 24 hours; Stress is projected to build from the mid-20s toward the upper-40s across the 12:30-14:00 UTC Retail Sales / UMich sentiment cluster and the US cash-open/power-hour window before easing back through the evening and into the quiet Saturday handover, with no forecast slot currently implying an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to stay in the low-to-medium-low band throughout, reflecting the continued Alpha Vantage outage and repeated stale futures print.

South Korean/US semiconductor names firmed overnight (Samsung, SK Hynix higher) and Nvidia reversed higher in premarket; no negative index-level semiconductor catalyst identified. Final hour before the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print; Stress continues to build on forecast dispersion and event positioning, consistent with treating pre-event anticipation as a Stress rather than Tail driver.

Retail Sales (12:30 UTC) prints within this hour, the session's first major checkpoint; Stress rises toward the elevated band on event/whipsaw risk around the release, while Tail requires an observed failed-pullback/persistent-extension reaction before it could follow, which is not yet asserted.

University of Michigan preliminary sentiment (14:00 UTC) prints within this hour on the heels of Retail Sales, keeping the window in event/whipsaw mode; Stress is projected to peak here before easing through the afternoon as the data cluster clears.
